chapter: Guitar, John Collins and Ellington on the radio
title: Chicago radio disc jockeys and Two Ton Baker playing Ellington
summary: Hearing Ellington and Lunceford through disc jockey Bob Hawk and pianist Two Ton Baker.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Well, did you get around as a teenager to hear much music in Chicago? Were you aware of who all was playing while you were in your teens?

Well, not so -- yes, I did, by record. There were disc jockeys there. There was one named Bob Hawk. I don't know whether he's around now or not, and he used to play Ellington quite a bit. And he played Lunceford. And there was a fellow that played piano. His name was Dick Baker, Two Ton Baker.
And he could play Ellington on piano, I mean play the arrangements on piano.

He had it down. He had it together. And I would catch him every morning, and as time went along that kind of listening began to just turn my mind around. But the Ellington situation was the thing that did it.
